teaser: Five invented users, a model reading screenshots, and a real browser: how to run synthetic users, from three studies.
core_idea: Synthetic users are invented people, each a record with a situation, a question, what they know and do not, what they decide on and what makes them leave, played by a model that drives a real browser one screenshot at a time instead of reading the page's code, so it can get lost as a person would. Claude Sonnet is good enough to play each user; the study lives in a GitHub repository or a vault shared by a link. Choose five to ten users of about five types, write profiles and expected journeys first, run the observe-think-act loop, interview and rate, order findings by cost, check every surprising finding against the browser's record, publish and run again. On newsroom.sgit.ai five readers produced 31 findings, six blocking; two were caused by the helper, and one became a measured bug: 51 of 527 figures missing.

nodes.label: Screenshot, not the code
nodes.summary: An agent reading the code finds every link and therefore no confusion.

nodes.label: A profile is a record
nodes.summary: Situation, question, knows, does not know, decides on, walks away if, patience, screen.

nodes.label: Expected journey first
nodes.summary: Written before the run, so a surprise shows as a difference.

nodes.label: Sonnet plays each user
nodes.summary: Good enough to read a screenshot and stay in character; Opus for checking evidence.

nodes.label: Repository or vault
nodes.summary: Public GitHub is easiest to share; a vault is encrypted, opens as an app, shared by a link.

nodes.label: Interview and rating
nodes.summary: The same ten questions for everyone; a rating from 1 to 5.

nodes.label: Findings ordered by cost
nodes.summary: Blocks a pilot, costs a payment, costs trust, loses a reader, minor.

nodes.label: Check before publishing
nodes.summary: Two newsroom findings were the helper's doing and are labelled, not deleted.

nodes.label: 51 of 527 figures missing
nodes.summary: The researcher's broken image, measured across the newsroom after the move.

nodes.label: Run against a verified copy
nodes.summary: Byte-identical local files: nothing reaches the live site, and the run repeats.

nodes.label: Three studies
nodes.summary: store.sgit.ai, riskmandate.ai and newsroom.sgit.ai, each in a vault.

quotes.text: An agent that reads the code finds every link every time, and so finds no confusion, which is the only thing worth running this for.
A findings list that silently loses items cannot be compared with the next one.
quotes.why: Why artefacts are labelled, not deleted.

quotes.text: Every site gets five users before it is called done, and the same five again after the fixes.

figures.caption: The newsroom study as it opens: five invented readers on the left, each with an outcome, the counts across all of them at the top, and the disclosure that everybody in it is invented before you can scroll past it.
The eight steps, with what we used for each on the newsroom. The first three are written before anything runs.
One of the newsroom profiles, field by field. The two fields shaded amber, what they do not know and what makes them leave, are the ones that make a run honest.

Step 1 of the retired teacher's run. The screenshot is the citation for everything she says next to it: a pound sign at the very top before she has read a thing, and her question, whether it is something she has been charged, given, or must pay.
The commuter's first screen, 390 by 844, exactly as the browser showed it. He read the £5.00 as a price.
The retired teacher's interview. "I half believed it": the reassurance landed, and then the line saying the cart was simulated made her wonder how carefully it is all run.
Everything they found on the newsroom, grouped by severity, each tagged with what it costs, the page, and the run that found it.
The researcher's step 12 on newsroom.sgit.ai: "screenshot unavailable (app-email-m60.webp)", and below it a dark box with only the image's description in it.
The three studies side by side, counted from the run records in each vault.
